company.description: India's largest integrated specialty fluorochemicals company and one of the first refrigerant makers in India (since 1967, 'Mafron' brand). Three verticals: High Performance Products (HPP: refrigerant gases R22/R32, HFO made for Honeywell, anhydrous and diluted hydrofluoric acid, inorganic fluorides such as BF3); Specialty Chemicals (fluorinated intermediates for agrochemical and pharma innovators, mostly multi-year contracts and campaigns run in multi-purpose plants); and CDMO (contract development and manufacturing for pharma under the Navin Molecular brand, mainly late-stage and commercial intermediates). It is incubating a fourth vertical, Advanced Materials (data-centre cooling fluids, electronic-grade HF, semiconductor and defence materials). Plants at Surat (Bhestan), Dahej (via NFASL), Dewas (CDMO cGMP plants) and a lab at Runcorn, UK. 66% of FY26 revenue came from outside India (USA ₹761 cr).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Navin Fluorine International (consolidated, ₹ crore). The company reports one segment and does not disclose EBITDA by business, so the model runs on one revenue line and one EBITDA margin. Revenue growth is built bottom-up from the three disclosed business verticals (see businessLines, which the authoring script checks against the model). Treasury income = yield × net cash; income on the existing investment book (held while gross debt is still outstanding) and interest on that debt are entered separately. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

businessLines._why: Bottom-up build of revenue (₹ crore). Sum of the three lines = model revenue (checked by the authoring script). FY26 actuals from the annual report.
businessLines._hppWhy: FY27 +27%: Q1 ₹540 cr (+33%) on AHF sales (plant commissioned Feb-2026), higher R32 volumes and prices; Q2-Q3 are seasonally softer for refrigerants; the new 15,000 tpa R32-equivalent plant starts in Q3FY27 (small FY27 contribution). FY28 +18%: the new plant at ~60% utilisation adds ~₹450-500 cr (management's 'downside case' peak revenue is ₹600-825 cr), partly offset by softer R32 prices in calendar 2027, India's 'free year' before HFC quotas, when new Indian capacity can sell. FY29 +12%: quota freeze from Jan-2028 supports prices; new plant near full use; Honeywell HFO flat (contract to 2029, extendable by three years at Honeywell's option).
businessLines._specialtyWhy: FY27 +25%: Q1 ₹325 cr (+48%); management sees ~80% utilisation of agro MPPs, campaign orders for 4-5 new agro molecules (3 patented); Dahej MPP debottleneck (₹75 cr, peak ₹140-160 cr) commissioned 29-Sep-2026; Project Nectar (₹540 cr dedicated plant) ramping to 75-80% by end-FY28. FY28 +16% / FY29 +14%: Nectar and MPP for a full year; Chemours liquid-cooling plant ramps over ~15 months; agro pricing stays weak (LatAm oversupply).
businessLines._cdmoWhy: FY27 +50%: management targets US$100 mn (~₹870 cr); Q1 ₹180 cr (+82%). We assume ₹820 cr (about 95% of target): cGMP4 phase 1 (commissioned Q3FY26) for the darolutamide intermediate supplied to Fermion (Orion/Bayer's Nubeqa). FY28 +25% / FY29 +18%: cGMP4 phase 2 (₹125 cr, Q4FY27); management talks of ~3x asset turn on the ₹288 cr cGMP4 (~₹860 cr) by FY29, plus the older cGMP1-3 plants; 3-4 molecules await FDA read-outs in 8-12 months (one recent read-out failed).

assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build: FY27E ₹4,305 cr (+30%), FY28E ₹5,110 cr (+19%), FY29E ₹5,820 cr (+14%). Management guides a 20-25% revenue CAGR to FY30 (analyst meet 20-Aug-2026, per PL and Axis); our FY25-29 CAGR is ~25%, front-loaded into FY26-27. Street FY27E revenue ₹4,165-4,714 cr, FY28E ₹4,933-5,862 cr.
assumptions._marginWhy: 32.6% in FY26; 34.2% in Q1FY27 and Q4FY26. Management guided 'in the range of 32-33%, plus/minus 1%' for the next one to two years (5-Aug-2026 call), after 'around 30%, ±1-2%' in April. FY27 33%: Q1 strong, but gross margin fell ~100bp QoQ on raw-material inflation and new plants carry start-up costs. FY28 32%: softer R32 prices in the 2027 free year, partly offset by CDMO mix. FY29 32.5%: quota regime and operating leverage. Street 31-33.6%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Management guided ~₹700 cr of capex in FY27 and ₹700-1,000 cr a year in FY28-FY30 (analyst meet 20-Aug-2026, per PL and Axis notes): R32 (₹236.5 cr), cGMP4 phase 2 (₹125 cr), advanced-materials adoption plant (₹90 cr), Chemours (₹120 cr, 35% customer-funded), cGMP5/6 infrastructure. FY26 actual ₹489 cr (Screener cash flow).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹149 cr ≈ 4.2% of average gross block (₹3,539 cr); Q1FY27 ₹41.7 cr (₹167 cr annualised) on a ~₹3,950 cr block.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to net cash (cash and investments less borrowings): ~₹54 cr at Mar-26 (the company turned net-debt-free in Q1FY27); builds from free cash flow.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Income on the gross investment book (₹1,229 cr of investments at Mar-26, mostly the Jul-2025 QIP money) held while ₹1,226 cr of debt is still outstanding, plus forex and misc. Q1FY27 ₹35 cr (FY26 ₹58 cr after a ₹6.75 cr exceptional charge). Falls as the investments are used to repay debt.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (term loans / ECBs for the Dahej projects, leases)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹118 cr; Q1FY27 ₹32 cr. Gross borrowings ₹1,226 cr at Mar-26 (₹940 cr non-current, ₹286 cr current); we assume steady repayment (PL assumes debt falls to ~₹490 cr by FY28).
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 24.0%; Q1FY27 23.6%; new regime 25.2% less incentives.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹15.1 a share (interim ₹6.5 + final ₹8.6) ≈ 12% of consolidated EPS; the company's standalone payout was 16%.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical refrigerant prices plus lumpy CDMO and agro campaigns; market-like sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Fluorochemicals, pharma outsourcing and advanced materials grow with global industrial and healthcare spend; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: ≈ nominal growth in end markets plus share gains; the HFC phase-down caps refrigerant volumes after 2032.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: R32 prices hold through the 2027 free year and India's 2028 quota freeze; CDMO beats the US$100 mn target on Nubeqa and new FDA approvals; Chemours and advanced materials scale early; margin ~34%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: New Indian R32 capacity floods the market in calendar 2027 and prices fall towards the US$5-6/kg 'downside case'; a CDMO molecule fails or Fermion orders pause; agro intermediates stay under Chinese price pressure; margin ~29%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Navin (ICICI Securities 45x, PL 41x, MOFSL 40x, Axis 34x FY28E EPS; Nuvama 40x Q1FY29E; JM 40x Jun-28E). 36x = Navin's ~45x one-year-forward median since 2021, cut by the ~19% de-rating of Indian chemical stocks versus their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. Our FY26-28 EPS growth (~27% a year) is in line with the street's, so no further growth adjustment; growth slows to ~16% in FY29.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Navin's trailing EV/EBITDA median since 2021 is ~40x; less the same ~19% de-rating ≈ 33x trailing, which is ~23x on Sep-28E EBITDA (about 1.4x the twelve months to Jun-26). Separates the business from the (small) net cash.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%. Heavy capex (₹700-1,000 cr a year) keeps free cash flow low for three years.

cover.headline: Three engines firing at once, and a price that already assumes they keep firing
cover.lead: Navin Fluorine makes refrigerant gases and hydrofluoric acid (HPP, 49% of FY26 revenue), fluorinated intermediates for agrochemical and pharma innovators (specialty, 35%) and pharma ingredients under contract (CDMO, 16%). After two flat years, five years of capex started to pay in FY26: revenue +41%, net profit +130%, EBITDA margin 32.6%; Q1FY27 added +44% and +108%. The street values the stock on **P/E on FY28E earnings (34-45x)**. Applying **36x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹225.9** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** The business is excellent; the price already pays for it. The cross-checks agree or are lower (EV/EBITDA ₹8,025, DCF ₹4,076). Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: All three businesses are growing fast
arguments.p: Q1FY27: HPP ₹540 cr (+33%), specialty ₹325 cr (+48%), CDMO ₹180 cr (+82%). New capacity arrives every quarter of FY27: AHF (Feb-2026), Dahej MPP debottleneck (29-Sep-2026), 15,000 t of R32 (Q3), Chemours (end-Q2), cGMP4 phase 2 (Q4).

arguments.h: The refrigerant boom has an expiry date
arguments.p: China's R32 price hit a decade high in Jun-2026 (CNY62,700-65,500/t) and India's HFC quotas freeze from Jan-2028 on 2024-26 output. But calendar 2027 is a "free year": anyone with capacity may sell, and ~81 kt of new Indian R32 capacity is coming (HSBC). Management itself says India will be "oversupplied for five years". We assume softer prices in FY28.

arguments.h: Great customers, but few of them
arguments.p: Three customers were 39% of FY26 revenue. The CDMO business rests on one molecule for one partner (the darolutamide intermediate for Fermion), Chemours has one plant (Navin's), and the Honeywell HFO contract runs to 2029. These contracts are the moat, and also the risk.

At ₹8,245 the stock trades at 39.6x our FY28E EPS, close to the street's 40x average and 4% below its record weekly close. Navin's one-year-forward P/E has a ~45x median since 2021, and Indian chemical stocks have de-rated ~19%; 36x gives {{dcf.upside|chg}}. We would buy below ~₹7,070.

sections.title: One fluorine platform, three businesses that look nothing alike

blocks.p: Everything Navin makes starts with fluorine. It buys fluorspar (mostly imported), turns it into hydrofluoric acid (HF) at Surat and now Dahej, and uses that HF three ways. **HPP** sells HF itself, refrigerant gases (R22 and R32 under the Mafron brand), inorganic fluorides such as boron trifluoride, and an HFO (a new low-global-warming refrigerant/blowing agent) made only for Honeywell under a US$410 mn contract. **Specialty chemicals** makes fluorinated building blocks for agrochemical and pharma innovators, mostly as campaigns in multi-purpose plants (MPPs) plus one dedicated plant (Project Nectar) for a marquee customer. **CDMO** (Navin Molecular, Dewas) makes advanced intermediates for drug companies under contract, mainly for Fermion (part of Orion), which makes darolutamide, the active ingredient in Bayer's prostate-cancer drug Nubeqa. A fourth business, **advanced materials** (data-centre cooling fluid for Chemours, electronic-grade HF, defence materials), is being incubated.

sections.title: Refrigerants at a cyclical high, pharma outsourcing growing, agro still weak

blocks.p: Navin sells into three very different markets. **Refrigerants** are a regulated commodity: the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol caps production of HFCs (gases such as R32 used in air-conditioners) country by country. China, the biggest producer, has run on quotas since 2024, and its R32 price reached a decade high in mid-2026. India freezes HFC output from Jan-2028 at the 2024-26 average plus a share of old HCFC (R22) production, so producers raced to run plants flat out and add capacity before the freeze. **Pharma CDMO** grows with drug companies outsourcing and with "China plus one" sourcing, but each contract depends on one drug's success. **Agro intermediates** are recovering in volume after the 2023-25 destocking, but prices remain under Chinese pressure.

sections.title: HPP: ₹1,615 cr of revenue riding the refrigerant cycle

blocks.p: HPP is half of Navin and the main reason for the FY26 profit jump. sections.title: Specialty chemicals: volume up, prices flat, plants filling

blocks.p: Specialty chemicals makes fluorinated intermediates (key starting materials) for global agrochemical companies and some pharma customers. It is a campaign business: a customer orders a few hundred tonnes of a molecule, Navin runs it in a multi-purpose plant for weeks, then switches to the next. Revenue fell 6% in FY25 as the global agro industry destocked, then rose 44% in FY26 to ₹1,152 cr as the Dahej plants filled and 13 new molecules were added. Q1FY27 was ₹325 cr (+48%), below the ₹354-360 cr of the previous two quarters because of campaign timing.

sections.title: CDMO: one blockbuster drug, a US$100 mn target and a lot of concentration

blocks.p: CDMO (contract development and manufacturing) means making drug intermediates to a pharma customer's recipe under strict quality rules (cGMP). Navin's CDMO revenue has swung wildly: ₹448 cr in FY23, ₹262 cr in FY24 (−42%), ₹546 cr in FY26 (+59%) and ₹180 cr in Q1FY27 alone (+82%). The swing factor is a multi-year contract signed in FY24 with Fermion, Orion's API unit, for an intermediate of darolutamide (Bayer/Orion's Nubeqa), a prostate-cancer drug that the CFO says could reach ~US$5 bn of peak sales. Navin built a dedicated block in cGMP4 (₹288 cr approved Feb-2024; phase 1 running since Q3FY26) and has started phase 2 (₹125 cr, ready Q4FY27). It is also moving one step closer to the final drug (API-minus-1) and working on an early-stage molecule for the same customer.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Navin has a **real but narrow moat**. Handling HF and fluorination safely at scale is hard, global innovators (Honeywell, Bayer's supply chain via Fermion, Chemours) have chosen it as a sole or main supplier, and from 2028 the HFC quota will keep new entrants out of refrigerants. But it has **no pricing power** in agro intermediates or in R32 during the 2027 free year, and its best contracts are concentrated in a handful of customers. That deserves a premium to commodity chemical makers, not a pharma-CDMO multiple across the whole business.

sections.title: Two flat years, then profit more than doubled in FY26

blocks.p: Navin Fluorine's revenue grew from ₹742 cr in FY17 to ₹2,077 cr in FY23, about 19% a year, as the company added specialty chemicals, contract manufacturing (CDMO) and the HFO plant built for Honeywell. Then it stalled: revenue was flat in FY24 (₹2,065 cr) and grew 14% in FY25, while new plants added depreciation and interest, so net profit fell from ₹375 cr (FY23) to ₹270-289 cr. FY26 was the breakout: revenue +41% to ₹3,314 cr, EBITDA doubled to ₹1,082 cr and net profit rose 130% to ₹664 cr, as refrigerant prices rose, CDMO grew 59% and the Dahej plants filled up. Q1FY27 kept going: revenue +44%, profit +108%.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** FY26 was not a lucky year; it was the year five years of capex (₹3,125 cr over FY22-26) started to earn. The CFO attributes ~70% of the 990bp margin gain to volumes from new capacity and ~30% to pricing. But part of the pricing is the refrigerant cycle (China R32 at a decade high in 2026), which will not last forever, and Navin does not disclose profit by business, so investors cannot see how much of the margin is cyclical.

sections.title: ₹3,125 cr of capex in five years: returns have only just caught up

blocks.p: Over FY22-26 Navin generated ₹2,226 cr of operating cash but spent ₹3,125 cr on plants (the Honeywell HFO plant, Dahej multi-purpose plants, Project Nectar, two R32 plants, the AHF plant and cGMP4) and ₹310 cr on dividends. The gap was funded first with debt (borrowings rose from ₹25 cr in FY21 to ₹1,466 cr in FY25) and then with a ₹750 cr share sale (QIP) in July 2025. Returns collapsed while the plants were being built (ROCE 11% in FY24-25) and recovered to 21% in FY26. The next leg needs ₹700-1,000 cr a year of capex again (FY27-30 guidance).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit and real cash, but too little disclosure by business

bullets: **No profit by business.** Navin reports one segment and discloses only revenue by vertical. Investors cannot see whether the FY26 margin jump came from refrigerant prices (cyclical) or CDMO (structural). The CFO's split (70% volumes, 30% pricing) is helpful but unaudited.
**Customer concentration.** Three customers were ₹545 cr, ₹391 cr and ₹342 cr of FY26 revenue (39% together); in FY25 one customer was 21%. Names are not disclosed.
**Cash conversion is good.** Operating cash flow ₹894 cr in FY26 (83% of EBITDA) and ₹173 cr in Q1FY27; net working capital fell to 74 days.
**Exceptional items are small.** FY26: −₹20.5 cr Labour Codes charge in Q3 and +₹13.7 cr credit in Q4 (not explained in what we read); net −₹6.8 cr.
**Customer-funded capex.** Contract liabilities of ₹212 cr are advances for the Chemours and Nectar plants: genuine commitment, but revenue still to be delivered.
**Other income** (₹65 cr in FY26, ₹35 cr in Q1FY27) is mostly treasury income on the QIP money; it falls as debt is repaid.
**FY20 profit (₹409 cr) was flattered by a negative tax charge** (tax rate −56% on Screener); it is not a comparable base.
**Depreciation** is ~4.2% of gross block, similar to SRF (4.6%): no sign of under-depreciation.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit (Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP) is clean, there are no restatements and the business converts profit into cash. The amber is for disclosure: with one reported segment and three customers making up ~40% of revenue, outsiders have to take the mix of cyclical and structural profit on trust.

sections.title: Net-debt-free after the QIP; working capital back under control

blocks.p: At March 2026 Navin had ₹1,226 cr of borrowings (term loans and ECBs taken for the Dahej projects, mostly in the subsidiary NFASL) and ₹1,321 cr of cash and current investments, mostly the QIP money, so net debt was almost nil (0.01x equity). The company says it became net-debt-free during Q1FY27. Working capital improved sharply: net working capital fell to 74 days of sales in FY26 from 90 days, and management now guides 75-80 days. Inventory days peaked at 197 in FY23 (when new plants were stocking up) and are 121 now.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Navin Fluorine International (consolidated, ₹ crore). The company reports one segment and does not disclose EBITDA by business, so the model runs on one revenue line and one EBITDA margin. Revenue growth is built bottom-up from the three disclosed business verticals (see businessLines, which the authoring script checks against the model). Treasury income = yield × net cash; income on the existing investment book (held while gross debt is still outstanding) and interest on that debt are entered separately. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

businessLines._why: Bottom-up build of revenue (₹ crore). Sum of the three lines = model revenue (checked by the authoring script). FY26 actuals from the annual report.
businessLines._hppWhy: FY27 +27%: Q1 ₹540 cr (+33%) on AHF sales (plant commissioned Feb-2026), higher R32 volumes and prices; Q2-Q3 are seasonally softer for refrigerants; the new 15,000 tpa R32-equivalent plant starts in Q3FY27 (small FY27 contribution). FY28 +18%: the new plant at ~60% utilisation adds ~₹450-500 cr (management's 'downside case' peak revenue is ₹600-825 cr), partly offset by softer R32 prices in calendar 2027, India's 'free year' before HFC quotas, when new Indian capacity can sell. FY29 +12%: quota freeze from Jan-2028 supports prices; new plant near full use; Honeywell HFO flat (contract to 2029, extendable by three years at Honeywell's option).
businessLines._specialtyWhy: FY27 +25%: Q1 ₹325 cr (+48%); management sees ~80% utilisation of agro MPPs, campaign orders for 4-5 new agro molecules (3 patented); Dahej MPP debottleneck (₹75 cr, peak ₹140-160 cr) commissioned 29-Sep-2026; Project Nectar (₹540 cr dedicated plant) ramping to 75-80% by end-FY28. FY28 +16% / FY29 +14%: Nectar and MPP for a full year; Chemours liquid-cooling plant ramps over ~15 months; agro pricing stays weak (LatAm oversupply).
businessLines._cdmoWhy: FY27 +50%: management targets US$100 mn (~₹870 cr); Q1 ₹180 cr (+82%). We assume ₹820 cr (about 95% of target): cGMP4 phase 1 (commissioned Q3FY26) for the darolutamide intermediate supplied to Fermion (Orion/Bayer's Nubeqa). FY28 +25% / FY29 +18%: cGMP4 phase 2 (₹125 cr, Q4FY27); management talks of ~3x asset turn on the ₹288 cr cGMP4 (~₹860 cr) by FY29, plus the older cGMP1-3 plants; 3-4 molecules await FDA read-outs in 8-12 months (one recent read-out failed).

assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build: FY27E ₹4,305 cr (+30%), FY28E ₹5,110 cr (+19%), FY29E ₹5,820 cr (+14%). Management guides a 20-25% revenue CAGR to FY30 (analyst meet 20-Aug-2026, per PL and Axis); our FY25-29 CAGR is ~25%, front-loaded into FY26-27. Street FY27E revenue ₹4,165-4,714 cr, FY28E ₹4,933-5,862 cr.
assumptions._marginWhy: 32.6% in FY26; 34.2% in Q1FY27 and Q4FY26. Management guided 'in the range of 32-33%, plus/minus 1%' for the next one to two years (5-Aug-2026 call), after 'around 30%, ±1-2%' in April. FY27 33%: Q1 strong, but gross margin fell ~100bp QoQ on raw-material inflation and new plants carry start-up costs. FY28 32%: softer R32 prices in the 2027 free year, partly offset by CDMO mix. FY29 32.5%: quota regime and operating leverage. Street 31-33.6%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Management guided ~₹700 cr of capex in FY27 and ₹700-1,000 cr a year in FY28-FY30 (analyst meet 20-Aug-2026, per PL and Axis notes): R32 (₹236.5 cr), cGMP4 phase 2 (₹125 cr), advanced-materials adoption plant (₹90 cr), Chemours (₹120 cr, 35% customer-funded), cGMP5/6 infrastructure. FY26 actual ₹489 cr (Screener cash flow).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹149 cr ≈ 4.2% of average gross block (₹3,539 cr); Q1FY27 ₹41.7 cr (₹167 cr annualised) on a ~₹3,950 cr block.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to net cash (cash and investments less borrowings): ~₹54 cr at Mar-26 (the company turned net-debt-free in Q1FY27); builds from free cash flow.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Income on the gross investment book (₹1,229 cr of investments at Mar-26, mostly the Jul-2025 QIP money) held while ₹1,226 cr of debt is still outstanding, plus forex and misc. assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (term loans / ECBs for the Dahej projects, leases)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹118 cr; Q1FY27 ₹32 cr. Gross borrowings ₹1,226 cr at Mar-26 (₹940 cr non-current, ₹286 cr current); we assume steady repayment (PL assumes debt falls to ~₹490 cr by FY28).
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 24.0%; Q1FY27 23.6%; new regime 25.2% less incentives.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹15.1 a share (interim ₹6.5 + final ₹8.6) ≈ 12% of consolidated EPS; the company's standalone payout was 16%.

methods.why: How the street values Navin (ICICI Securities 45x, PL 41x, MOFSL 40x, Axis 34x FY28E EPS; Nuvama 40x Q1FY29E; JM 40x Jun-28E). 36x = Navin's ~45x one-year-forward median since 2021, cut by the ~19% de-rating of Indian chemical stocks versus their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. Our FY26-28 EPS growth (~27% a year) is in line with the street's, so no further growth adjustment; growth slows to ~16% in FY29.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Navin's trailing EV/EBITDA median since 2021 is ~40x; less the same ~19% de-rating ≈ 33x trailing, which is ~23x on Sep-28E EBITDA (about 1.4x the twelve months to Jun-26). Separates the business from the (small) net cash.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%. Heavy capex (₹700-1,000 cr a year) keeps free cash flow low for three years.
